source_text: Eius autem virtutis tunc constare rationem, si nullum subditorum puniret nisi pro his delictis, quae constabat libera voluntate commissa.
pass_a_gloss: But that the account of this virtue then stands, if he would punish none of those subject except for those offenses which stood established as committed by a free will.

lemmas.lexica: LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS liber=free; also children; context decides

pass_b_english: The character of this virtue would be maintained only if God punished none of those subject to him except for offenses established to have been committed by free will.

choices.why: Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.
For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
